# Largest-remainder allocation algorithm

> A mathematical algorithm that distributes a net amount proportionally across shops based on their line totals, ensuring the sum equals the exact net amount to the cent with no rounding loss.

_Part of [Settling paid orders to shops](settling-orders-to-shops.md)_

When an order with multiple shops is paid, the net amount (total minus platform fee) must be split across the shops that fulfilled it. Simply dividing proportionally can leave a few cents unaccounted for due to rounding. The largest-remainder allocation algorithm solves this: it calculates each shop's proportional share, then systematically gives any remaining cents to the shops with the largest fractional parts. The result is an array of amounts that sum exactly to the net amount—not a penny more or less. In [Settling paid orders to shops](settling-orders-to-shops.md), when an `order.paid` event arrives, the settlement listener groups line totals by shop, sorts shops alphabetically for determinism, and calls `allocate()` with the net amount and each shop's total. It gets back an array of allocated amounts, one per shop in sorted order. This array then becomes the credit side of a SETTLEMENT journal: each shop account is credited with its allocated share.

**Look at:** [`allocate` in settlement.listener.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/settlement.listener.ts#L9)

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| event | `order.paid` | Triggers settlement; contains order total, platform fee, shop line items, and payment id |
| database | `SETTLEMENT journal (LedgerEntry rows)` | One line debits CLEARING by the net amount; one line per shop credits that shop with its allocated share |

## Watch out

- All amounts are integers in cents; no floating-point math, so rounding must be solved algorithmically.
- Shops are sorted before allocation to ensure deterministic output—the same inputs always produce the same share order.
- The net amount is already reduced by the platform fee before allocation; the platform fee is not distributed across shops.
- If an order has no shop line items, settlement is skipped (the function returns early and no journal is posted).
